principles: Criterion: PACKET's EXTRACT_PROMPT sentence, applied to each document's own text only. Guide and notes of one technology were adjudicated separately and may differ (e.g. msw worker.stop() is breaking+required in the guide, which says to await it, and neither in the notes, which say awaiting matters only for in-flight cases). Items that neither labeler listed were not added, but unlabelled lines that restate a labelled change were added as anchors (e.g. the kit guide's 'Removed options' bullet for csrf.checkOrigin, the kit notes' duplicate remote-types and 'nested server-only directories' bullets).

Same change, several spans (a heading and its paragraph, a summary sentence and its section, a 'Removed options' list and its own section, a code-step sentence such as 'Use X instead' or 'please update imports accordingly'): one item whose anchors list every verbatim single-line span describing it. A change stated twice as separate bullets in release notes (Node 22 / Node 22.17, Vite 8 / vite@^8.0.12, TypeScript 5.9 minimum / TypeScript 5.1-5.2 dropped) is one item with both anchors.

Granularity: one bullet or sentence announcing several changes gives several items sharing one group (base/assets/resolveRoute; Server + SSRManifest; $lib->#lib + files.lib; transformers TrainingArguments bullets naming two arguments). Different sentences of one paragraph are separate groups (msw onUnhandledFrame rename vs. its WebSocket scope; kit preloadData error result vs. redirect status; linkHeaderPreload option vs. its default), and each is anchored on its own sentence where the line also carries another change. A heading summarising several bullets (transformers '5. Removed legacy configuration file saving:') is attached as a shared anchor to each bullet's item.

required (PACKET): true when the document tells the upgrader to act (replace/rename/must/should be removed/use Y instead/pass ... instead), for any removal, rename or raised minimum, and when the text makes clear that unchanged code now fails (an error, a rejection, a failed type check: e.g. mypy strict-bytes, non-ASCII cookie names, goto rejecting, x-sveltekit- query params, msw file:// and fetch upgrade requests now throwing). Conditional steps ('if you use X', 'for runtimes that ...', 'if you want to avoid that') are required. False for a behaviour change the document describes but asks no action for (cookie management, delta, handleError receiving all errors, config precedence, dev CORS), even when breaking; such labeler 'unsure (required)' flags were removed as settled by PACKET.

unsure (required) is kept only where the text changes something existing code consumes without saying to act or that it fails: return-shape changes (transformers decode, apply_chat_template), renames stated only as 'previously known as' or 'merged into' (PythonBackend, MistralCommonBackend, SpecialTokensMixin), files or modules whose new semantics may break imports (server-only directories, slow/fast tokenizer files, generated tsconfig location), and default flips whose effect is not stated (mypy --local-partial-types). Best guesses are recorded in `required`.

unsure (qualifies) is kept for opaque commit-style entries with no stated user effect (mypy parallel-checking internals, 'minor fixes', 'better logging', 'consistent special filename patterns'), implementation-level performance work, dependency swaps that may be skip-list chores (msw dependency removals and @msw/url, mypy ast-serialize), known-issue disclaimers (transformers RC0 MoE notes), and APIs a document mentions without saying they are new (msw defineNetwork, convert_from_spm). A labeler's unsure flag was dropped when the text shows a user-visible effect: support for new runtime/TypeScript/GraphQL versions, changed diagnostics text, named performance effects, fixes to user-visible behaviour. One A-only item was dropped: transformers' weekly-release cadence (project news, skip list).

unsure (breaking) is kept only where the text does not show whether existing code behaves differently in a noticeable way (mypy no longer narrowing final globals, transformers 50GB shards and compute_loss_func priority, kit form.error/remote error typing, kit version-polling pragma header). Otherwise the rubric's last sentence settles it: a new optional option, a deprecation, a narrowed type existing code already satisfies (resolve() always a Promise) or a sync function that awaiting callers still handle (getRequest/setResponse) is not breaking; a removal (including a removed response header) is.

change_type: removals, renames, moved modules/types and raised minimums are removal; a module made importable in a new context is other; a new accepted input form on an existing feature (matcher functions/schemas, hyphens in names, passthrough header modification) is new_option; changed diagnostics and changed narrowing/inference are behavior_change; tsconfig requirements are tooling; leaving an experimental namespace is stability_change; opt-in hardening against misuse (external redirects) is security; 'generated by default' and dev-time default flips are default_change.
